title: Være eller bli — a state or a change
goal: Choose være for a stable state and bli for a change into a new state.

objectives.statement: Choose være for a stable state and bli for a change into a new state.

sections.title: A room that is not ready yet

spans.value: Mina and Jonas are preparing a room at a community centre for an evening concert. The guests arrive in an hour.
Ja, men det blir snart varmt. Jeg har slått på ovnen.

blocks.translation: Yes, but it will soon get warm. I have turned on the heater.
Good. The tables are dirty too.

spans.value: Jeg vasker dem. Da blir de rene.

blocks.translation: I’ll wash them. Then they’ll become clean.

spans.value: Den blir lysere når jeg slår på lampen.

blocks.translation: It will get brighter when I turn on the lamp.

spans.value: Flott. Jeg er litt stresset nå, men jeg blir roligere når alt er klart.

blocks.translation: Great. I’m a little stressed now, but I’ll become calmer when everything is ready.

In the adjective descriptions taught here, use
when you describe how someone or something is. You present the state as true at the time you are talking about.
An adjective state does not have to be permanent. Mina may be stressed for only ten minutes, but
still describes her present state. For this pattern, the important question is not whether the condition lasts forever. The question is whether you are describing the condition itself.
Mina enters a room that is already noisy. Describe its current condition in one Norwegian sentence using

In the adjective descriptions taught here, use

Each sentence has an implicit contrast between an earlier condition and a later one. The room was cold; after the heater is turned on, it becomes warm. Mina was stressed; as the preparations finish, she becomes calmer.

For the adjective descriptions in this lesson, ask one question before choosing the verb:
Am I describing an existing adjective state, or movement into a new adjective state?

In the second example, the coffee does not have to be completely cold yet. The sentence focuses on the development away from its earlier temperature.
The first sentence describes the children during a quiet moment. The second suggests a change: perhaps someone begins speaking, the music stops, or the teacher enters.
Complete mixed short situations by choosing

For example, contexts might show a room during a noisy moment, a room becoming quiet when a concert starts, a nervous performer at one moment, or a performer calming down on stage. Do not merely translate isolated sentences; use the contextual information to choose the verb.

sections.title: Time expressions can make the change clearer

spans.value: In adjective descriptions, words such as
(when) often help reveal the intended viewpoint. They do not choose the verb automatically, but they provide context.

en.value: The room will soon become warm.
Mina is stressed before the concert.

no.value: Hun blir roligere når gjestene kommer.

en.value: She becomes calmer when the guests arrive.
The tables will get dirty after the party.

spans.value: In the adjective descriptions taught here,
does not simply mark the future; it presents a change into a new adjective state. An adjective sentence with
may also refer to another time if the context makes that time clear. The relevant contrast remains an existing adjective state versus movement into one.

en.value: The hall is full during the concert.

no.value: Salen blir full når publikum kommer.

en.value: The hall fills up when the audience arrives.

spans.value: The first sentence describes the hall during the concert. The second follows the hall from less full to full.

sections.title: Using blir for every temporary adjective condition

spans.value: That sentence can be correct if the speaker means that illness begins today. It is not the normal choice for simply reporting a present condition.
Compare a context where change is intended:

sections.title: Guided practice: follow one object through time

spans.value: Choose one element from the concert room, such as the temperature, tables, lighting, hall, or Mina’s mood. Describe its initial state, the change caused by an event, and its state after the change.

sections.title: Broader practice: apply the contrast in new situations

spans.value: Write short connected descriptions for several everyday changes. Suitable contexts include a cold drink warming on a table, a quiet station becoming busy, or a worried friend calming down. In each description, include both an existing adjective state and a change into another adjective state.

prompt.value: Mina går inn i konsertsalen og merker at det allerede er støyende. Skriv en kort melding til Jonas om hvordan rommet er nå. Bruk er om tilstanden.

payload.judge_prompt: Check that the response describes the current room and uses er to express the existing adjective state.

criteria.instruction: Describes the room as already noisy at the moment of speaking.
Uses er to express the room's existing adjective state.
Observation only: note whether the response uses the taught er form; do not fail a natural equivalent.

prompt.value: Jonas slår på ovnen og lampene, vasker bordene og åpner gardinene. Skriv en kort melding på norsk til Mina med fire setninger. Beskriv hvordan rommet blir etter hver handling.

payload.judge_prompt: Check that the response covers all four actions and presents each result as a change into a new adjective state with blir.

criteria.instruction: Describes a plausible result of turning on the heater, turning on the lamps, washing the tables, and opening the curtains.
For each of the four actions, uses blir to present the result as a change into a new adjective state.
Observation only: note variation in adjective choice and wording; do not fail a natural equivalent.
